title: Introduce compact weight proxy and simplify tokenizer handshake to reduce model load tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight in-process 'compact weight proxy' that lazily resolves and exposes weight shards to the runtime, and simplify the tokenizer handshake to avoid blocking model activation on full vocab/materialization. The goal is to reduce model load tail latency (95th/99th percentiles) and eliminate several long-standing failure modes around mixed-format checkpoints and tokenizer mismatches.
background: We repeatedly see model startup tails when ingesting large sharded checkpoints and when tokenizers trigger synchronous vocab rebuilds during model activation. Historically we've used monolithic loaders that deserialize entire shard sets and perform tokenizer initialization inline, which hurts cold-start and redeploy latency and increases OOM risk for constrained Dedicated nodes. Multiple engineering tickets (listed in dependencies) explored pieces of this; this ticket consolidates the minimal, low-risk runtime changes to deliver measurable tail reduction and safer migration paths.
proposal: Implement a Compact Weight Proxy component that sits between the artifact loader and the executor. The proxy will: 1) present a canonical, page-aligned weight view to the runtime; 2) lazily materialize shard pages on first access; 3) keep small per-model metadata to enable quick validation without full weight reads. In parallel, change tokenizer initialization to a two-stage handshake: fast fingerprint check + lazy lexicon loader. Use a feature flag to enable the proxy per model and maintain backwards-compatible loader path. Avoid modifying on-disk checkpoint format: implement the proxy as a compatibility layer that understands existing manifests and shard layouts.
migration_plan: 1) Add Compact Weight Proxy code behind feature flag; 2) Wire model manifest parsing to return proxy-backed WeightHandles when feature flag on; 3) Update the runtime to tolerate page-fault-style callbacks from the proxy; 4) Release to canary traffic with limited model set; 5) Gradually expand; 6) Roll back by disabling feature flag if issues arise. For the tokenizer handshake: 1) Add vocab fingerprint to model metadata; 2) If fingerprint matches cached tokenizer, skip full rebuild; 3) Otherwise trigger lazy lexicon materialization on first tokenization call.
rollout_plan: Start with a canary fleet (5% of Dedicated capacity) and a selected set of internal models used for load testing. Monitor model activation time, 95/99 latency, memory churn during loads, and error rates. If stable after 48 hours, expand to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks. Keep an automatic fallback that disables the proxy for models that hit false positive validation or excessive page-miss rates.
testing_plan: Unit tests for proxy semantics (materialize-on-read, correct weight exposure), integration tests that boot real checkpoints with mixed formats, and fuzz tests for manifest edge cases. Create end-to-end tests that simulate constrained memory nodes and measure peak RSS and activation latency. Add a synthetic benchmark job that compares old path vs proxy: cold-start wall time, 95/99 activation latency, and memory high-water mark.
metrics: Monitor: model_activation_time_ms_p50,p95,p99; weight_materialization_io_ops_per_activation; memory_high_water_mark_mb; runtime_page_miss_rate; tokenizer_init_time_ms_p95; model_boot_errors_total. Targets: reduce activation p95 by >=20% and p99 by >=30% for checkpoint-heavy models, and cut tokenizer init p95 by >=50% for models with large lexicons.
risks: 1) Proxy bugs could expose incorrect weight values if materialization logic is flawed; mitigated by strict checksums and staged rollout. 2) Excessive page-miss I/O may increase latency for unexpected access patterns; mitigated by telemetry and dynamic eviction thresholds. 3) Tokenizer fingerprint mismatch edge-cases leading to behavioral differences; mitigated by opt-in testing and maintained backwards path.

acceptance_criteria: Compact Weight Proxy implemented behind a feature flag and integrated with manifest parsing
Unit and integration tests covering lazy materialization and checksum validation
Canary deployment demonstrating >=20% p95 activation reduction for targeted models
Tokenizer handshake updated to include fingerprint check and lazy lexicon loader
Documentation updated with migration steps and diagnostic dashboards
Rollback path validated (disable feature flag returns to previous behavior without model corruption)
